title: Build the Right Thing: Product Engineering (Part 1) — Kent C. Dodds, EpicProduct.engineer
talk_summary: Kent C. Dodds argues that as AI agents commoditize implementation, the scarce and durable skill becomes product judgment: deciding what to build, validating problems before building, and taking ownership of system design. The talk is mostly product-discovery frameworks (Mom Test, jobs theory, Kano) aimed at human engineers, not agent orchestration.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before building, require evidence of the actual problem: what users did instead, what it cost them, how often it happens — not 'would you use this'. Engineers push back on feature requests lacking this validation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if that feature request doesn't come with some sort of validation of why this exists, then you as a product engineer need to go back to the PM

takeaways.what_they_do: In the AI era the agent produces the whole thing; the human's job is to whittle it down to the minimal slice that demonstrates the problem is solved, and to launch in weeks not a year.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we probably could have launched something in two weeks, not a year and done the integration manually
takeaways.numbers: 1.2M AUD (~900k USD) spent over a year on a product nobody used

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues engineers take more care designing the 'playground' for agents when they know they'll be paged at 2am; ownership of edge cases and scalability is what separates real work from surface-level prototypes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you know that you're going to be paged at two in the morning to deal with issues, then you're going to take a lot of care

takeaways.what_they_do: Frames the lead engineer as responsible for making the system a good 'playground' for agents: good testing, clear architecture, obvious Lego blocks so agents make fewer mistakes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are now all team leads over however many agents you're able to run at once. And it's your job to make sure that that playground is a really nice playground
